findings.evidence: Section 2.3 states the canonical-host verdict: "prefill 1.29 PFLOP / (8 × 0.989 PFLOPS) = 0.16 s at peak, ~0.47 s at 35% MFU". Chapter 4 §4.3 repeats: "The modelled host prefill is ~0.16 s at peak and ~0.47 s at 35% MFU (Ch 2)". Chapter 6 §6.3.3 uses the same: "the 8×H100 sustained prefill capacity of ~2.77 PFLOP/s (35% MFU, Ch 8 §3)". But Chapter 4 §4.3 also states the implied single-request rate as: "The cap implies ≈8,500 tokens/s (9,200 ÷ 1.08 = 8,519): that is only the budget-implied single-request rate for a request that holds the whole host". Chapter 4 then computes "the 8-GPU host needs ~0.47 s (9,200 ÷ 19,780 = 0.465 s; 19,780 = 8 × 2,472.5 tok/s, the unrounded form of the ~19,800 tok/s planning rate)". So the same host is credited with both ~8,500 tok/s (budget-implied, ~1.08 s) and ~19,780 tok/s (35% MFU planning rate, ~0.47 s) — the book labels the 8,500 figure as 'only the budget-implied single-request rate for a request that holds the whole host' and warns not to divide by it. The two rates are distinguished in prose but appear on the same page of Ch 4 without a shared 'do not compare' warning at the point where the ~19,800 tok/s planning rate is itself used as a fleet-sizing denominator (Chapter 4 §4.6: 'prefill screens at ≥5 hosts at average (92,000 ÷ 19,800 = 4.65, ceiled)' and the mini-case at §4.8: '50 rps × 9,200 input = 460,000 prefill tokens/s ÷ ~19,800 tokens/s per host ... = 24 hosts').
findings.issue: Two materially different prefill rates for the same 8×H100 host (~8,500 tok/s budget-implied and ~19,800 tok/s at 35% MFU) coexist in Ch 4 §4.3 within a few paragraphs; the first is explicitly flagged as not-a-host-rate but the second is then used as a per-host fleet-sizing denominator in §4.6 and §4.8 without repeating the warning that it is a planning rate, not a measured or SLO-goodput rate.
findings.fix_instruction: At the point in §4.6 and §4.8 where ~19,800 tok/s is used as the per-host prefill denominator, restate in-line that this is the 35% MFU sustained-planning rate (a planning bound, not a measured goodput), and note the contrast with the ~8,500 tok/s budget-implied single-request rate so the two are not conflated by a reader scanning the chapter.

findings.evidence: §2.1.2 'Implementation note inspected on 28 October 2026 (post-cutoff addendum...) ... The pinned source establishes the execution pattern below, not a measurement of latency, memory use or service capacity.'
findings.issue: The book uses a future date (2026) for a 'post-cutoff addendum' in a section describing a specific implementation inspection. While consistent with the fictional future edition of the book, the phrase 'outside the 30 August 2026 evidence snapshot' combined with the specific date '28 October 2026' introduces a temporal inconsistency in the document's own 'current time' if not carefully read, as it describes an event happening after the 'First edition, 2026' publication date listed on the title page.
findings.fix_instruction: Add a footnote or clarification that the '2026' dates refer to the book's fictional 'current era' context, or verify that the 'First edition 2026' date on the cover implies these are post-publication updates. (Note: This is likely intentional world-building for the AI persona, but technically flagged as a temporal anomaly in a static document).
